concepts.why: The presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof and an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit suggests fibrous dysplasia of bone.
The finding of a heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof and an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit could also suggest an orbital osteoma.

The presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof and an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit could also suggest an orbital meningioma.

The finding of a heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof and an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit could also suggest Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof and an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit could also suggest eosinophilic granuloma.

rationales.F01: Long-standing swelling suggests a slow-growing process, consistent with fibrous dysplasia or Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F04: Rapid progression of proptosis suggests an aggressive process, consistent with orbital meningioma or fibrous dysplasia.
rationales.F07: Heterogeneous enhancing mass is highly suggestive of a neoplastic process, such as orbital meningioma or fibrous dysplasia.
rationales.F08: Expansive lytic bony lesion is highly suggestive of fibrous dysplasia or Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass and an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing supports fibrous dysplasia of bone, which is a condition known to cause such bony lesions and orbital displacement.
